messages:
Erin (Privacy): Hey team — we got a DSAR that requests deletion of user X's data across embeddings and logs. Two wrinkles: some embeddings are in the vector DB (managed by us) and some snapshots/backups live in S3 encrypted with the account KMS key. What's the minimal safe workflow to satisfy the DSAR and produce an audit trail?

Dave (EngSec): Thanks Erin. Short answer: 1) remove live records (vector DB + any index metadata); 2) mark and chain-delete any derived artifacts; 3) schedule snapshot pruning + explicit s3 object delete with kms-delete logs; 4) produce signed audit record. Need to flesh steps.

Alice (Infra): For backups: we currently run daily snapshots to s3://redwood-backups/ with lifecycle 90d. Snapshots are encrypted with aws:kms key alias/redwood-prod. Deleting objects is straightforward but if the object is in a cross-account replication bucket there are extra perms. Also need to ensure eventual consistency for the vector DB compaction job.

Ben (Legal): We need a verifiable audit trail that shows which objects were deleted and by whom, and when. A simply 'marked' row in DB isn't enough. Can we include checksums + object keys in the audit? Also need an attestation signed by EngSec for the customer.

Carol (Support): Customer asked for a completion ETA within 10 business days. We should confirm whether we need to contact them with a partial deletion status if backups will be pruned later.

Dave (EngSec): Proposal: create a DSAR runbook run with these stages: 
1) Identify all PII tokens/IDs in embeddings index (query by user id). 
2) Delete entries from vector DB via service API and log the request id. 
3) Trigger compaction + verify count delta. 
4) Find S3 objects (snapshots) containing user ID using manifest + generate list. 
5) Issue s3 delete-object calls for matching keys and record the S3 delete-object response (RequestCharged/ETag). 
6) Rotate or rewrap objects if KMS prevents deletion? (rare) 
7) Produce final signed JSON with all artifacts + hashes.

Erin (Privacy): That sounds good. Two Qs: a) do we have RBAC to allow Privacy ops to trigger #4/#5 without root creds? b) can we include KMS key usage logs in the audit (Decrypt/GenerateDataKey events)?

Alice (Infra): RBAC: currently only infra-admins and backup-service-role can delete from the backups bucket. We can add a scoped role 'dsar-processor' with assume-role permissions limited to DeleteObject on s3://redwood-backups/daily/* and ListBucket for manifests. That role would be auditable.

Dave (EngSec): +1 for scoped role. We should tie assumes to short-lived creds (STS) and require MFA for manual runs. Also log assume-role events to CloudTrail and ship to our audit index.

DevOps-Bot: Incident note created: IDS-2026-DSAR-1830002468, assigned to team eng-security.

Ben (Legal): KMS logs: CloudTrail shows kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey calls. However, if we're only deleting S3 objects (no decrypt), we get kms:ReEncryptFrom and KMS DeleteKey is rarely used. We should capture s3:DeleteObject and kms:GenerateDataKey/Decrypt events if any rewrap occurs. Those appear in CloudTrail and can be exported to the audit S3 prefix.

Carol (Support): For customer communication: propose "we've deleted live copies and scheduled backup pruning; full proof package will be delivered once backup objects are pruned and audit package assembled (ETA 7 days)". Legal ok with that?

Ben (Legal): Acceptable if we note the retention exception window and the exact items pending. Must include the manifests and signed hashes.

Dave (EngSec): Action items: 
- Alice to propose IAM policy and create dsar-processor role (deadline: 48h).
- Alice to add CloudTrail filter to capture s3:DeleteObject + kms events to audit bucket (48h).
- Erin to compile list of user identifiers and vector DB query + share runbook steps (today).
- Carol to send customer the interim notice (today).
- Dave to prepare signed audit JSON template and attach procedure for signing (72h).

Alice (Infra): Working on the IAM policy now. Quick Q: should dsar-processor be able to delete across historical snapshots or only snapshot manifests? If we allow object deletes we risk accidental mass deletes. Maybe require a manifest-based delete: only keys enumerated by the manifest can be deleted.

Erin (Privacy): Prefer manifest-based deletes — safer and easier to show proof. We'll provide the manifest extraction script.

Dave (EngSec): Agree on manifest-only. We'll add a pre-delete dry-run that outputs the would-be keys + checksums to the audit log; run must be approved by a second approver (2FA) before actual delete.

Carol (Support): I have a small ask: can we add a field to the DSAR ticket to capture 'backup-manifest-hash' so the customer letter references the exact manifest? That helps Legal.

Ben (Legal): Yes please. Also include redwood-signer identity and timestamp in the package.

Erin (Privacy): I'll prepare the manifest script and send to Alice. Expecting to test on staging today.

DevOps-Bot: Playbook updated: /runbooks/dsar-delete-manifest-v1 (draft).

Alice (Infra): IAM policy draft (snippet):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:ListBucket"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-backups"],"Condition":{"StringLike":{"s3:prefix":["daily/*/manifests/*"]}}},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:DeleteObject"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-backups/daily/*/manifests/*"],"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:RequestTag/DSAR":"true"}}}
  ]
}
```

Dave (EngSec): Nice. Add a kms:ViaService condition so we can tie deletes to the S3 service call path. Also make sure CloudTrail is parsing events into our SIEM index with the requestParameters.keyId and responseElements for ETag.

Alice (Infra): Will do. Deploying role to staging now.

Erin (Privacy): Thanks all — once we have the staging run validated, I'll open the DSAR ticket and request the run. Carol, proceed with interim notice.

Carol (Support): Sent interim reply to customer with ETA and note about backups. Ticket updated: #DSAR-9912.

Dave (EngSec): After this completes we should add an automated monthly audit to validate that DSAR manifests and deletion packages are stored immutable for 7 years per our retention for legal hold.

Ben (Legal): 7 years seems long for privacy. Let's cap audit storage at 2 years unless under legal hold. Update task for policy team.

Erin (Privacy): Noted. I'll sync with Policy. Thanks everyone. :pray:
